advances: Provides geometric and probabilistic lower bounds for the cubic moment using convex log-weight slabs, and gives necessary energy-spreading conditions for a vanishing normalized cubic moment.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None beyond the declared accepted predecessor.
proof:
Each \(D_j\) is complete in its intrinsic affine lattice: a lattice point in its convex hull lies in \(D\) and in the same slab. The strict upper endpoint causes no difficulty because a finite set of points strictly below that endpoint has its entire convex hull strictly below it.

Let \(q_j=p(\,\cdot\mid D_j)\). Restricting any containing halfspace to \(D_j\) gives
\[
\tau_p(\mathbf z)\ge\alpha_j\tau_{q_j}(\mathbf z)
\quad(\mathbf z\in D_j).
\]
All conditional probabilities in this slab have ratio at most \(e^L\), so
\(q_j\ge e^{-L}u_j\) pointwise and
\(\tau_{q_j}\ge e^{-L}\tau_{u_j}\). The center weight and three depth factors therefore give
\[
\sum_{\mathbf z\in D_j}p_{\mathbf z}\tau_p(\mathbf z)^3
\ge\alpha_j^4M_3(q_j)\ge e^{-4L}\alpha_j^4U_j.
\]
Summation proves (1). Hölder gives
\[
\left(\sum_{j\in J}\alpha_j\right)^4
\le
\left(\sum_{j\in J}\alpha_j^4U_j\right)
\left(\sum_{j\in J}U_j^{-1/3}\right)^3,
\]
proving (2).

Accepted fact 01a4100542206b94 gives \(U_j\ge8^{-r_j}/4\), where \(r_j\) is the intrinsic affine-lattice dimension of \(D_j\). A singleton has moment \(1\), so the weaker common bound \(U_j\ge8^{-N}/4\) holds for all slabs.

When \(\sigma>0\), Chebyshev places at least \(3/4\) of the probability in an interval of width \(4\sigma\). At most \(\lceil4\sigma\rceil\le1+4\sigma\) appropriately placed unit slabs cover that interval. Applying (1) and
\(\sum_{j=1}^K\alpha_j^4\ge(\sum_j\alpha_j)^4/K^3\)
proves (3). If \(\sigma=0\), the law is uniform and the accepted uniform bound is stronger.

The atomic inequality \(M_3\ge\sum p_{\mathbf z}^4\), combined with one quarter of (3), proves (4).

For a single interval, the same conditional-law proof applies directly, including closed endpoints, and gives
\(M_3\ge e^{-4L}p(\log p\in I)^4\,8^{-N}/4\).
This proves the concentration estimate. Rearranging (2) gives the inverse-moment budget.

If exactly two log-weight levels occur, each level is a complete support of affine dimension at most \(N-1\), and its conditional law is uniform. With level masses \(a,1-a\),
\[
M_3(p)\ge
\frac{8^{-(N-1)}}4\left(a^4+(1-a)^4\right)
\ge\frac14\,8^{-N}.
\]
Singleton level sets only improve this estimate.
statement:
Let \(D=\operatorname{conv}(D)\cap\mathbb Z^N\) be finite and nonempty, and let
\(p_{\mathbf z}=e^{\bm{\theta}\cdot\mathbf z}/Z_D(\bm{\theta})\).
Use actual closed-halfspace depth
\(\tau_p(\mathbf z)=\min_{H\ni\mathbf z}p(H)\) and
\(M_3(p)=\sum p_{\mathbf z}\tau_p(\mathbf z)^3\).

Partition the log-weights into slabs of width \(L>0\):
\[
D_j=\{\mathbf z:a+jL\le\log p_{\mathbf z}<a+(j+1)L\}.
\]
For each nonempty slab, let \(\alpha_j=p(D_j)\), let \(u_j\) be its uniform law, and let \(U_j=M_3(u_j)\). Then
\[
M_3(p)\ge e^{-4L}\sum_j\alpha_j^4U_j. \tag{1}
\]
For every collection \(J\) of slabs with total mass \(\rho>0\),
\[
M_3(p)\ge
e^{-4L}\frac{\rho^4}
{\left(\sum_{j\in J}U_j^{-1/3}\right)^3}. \tag{2}
\]

If \(\sigma^2=\operatorname{Var}_p(\log p_{\mathbf X})\), then
\[
M_3(p)\ge
\frac{81}{1024e^4(1+4\sigma)^3}8^{-N}, \tag{3}
\]
and
\[
M_3(p)\ge
\frac{81}{4096e^4(1+4\sigma)^3}8^{-N}
+\frac34\sum_{\mathbf z}p_{\mathbf z}^4. \tag{4}
\]

Writing \(\varepsilon=8^NM_3(p)\), every interval \(I\) of length \(L\) satisfies
\[
p\{\log p_{\mathbf X}\in I\}\le(4e^{4L}\varepsilon)^{1/4},
\]
and every slab collection of mass at least \(\rho\) satisfies
\[
2^{-N}\sum_{j\in J}U_j^{-1/3}
\ge e^{-4L/3}\rho^{4/3}\varepsilon^{-1/3}.
\]
Finally, a complete log-affine law with exactly two log-weight levels satisfies \(M_3(p)\ge8^{-N}/4\).
